language.script_notes: Rioplatense Spanish as national; Welsh-descended place names appear in parts of Chubut Province (a 19th-century Welsh settlement legacy).
false_friends: Chilean Patagonia (same mountains/steppe, opposite side of the Andes)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Minimal to absent on remote rural roads; present on mountain routes near the Andes.
road_furniture.line_paint: As national, though many roads are unpaved gravel (ripio) in remote stretches.
road_furniture.curb_style: Essentially absent outside small towns; wide open unpaved shoulders.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national; long, straight, empty roads with sparse signage are the norm.

architecture.roof_style: Steep-pitched roofs in the Andean lake district (Bariloche) reflecting Alpine/German-Swiss immigrant influence; simple low buildings in the steppe interior.
architecture.roof_material: Wood shingle and metal roofing in the mountain towns; corrugated metal on remote ranch (estancia) buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Alpine chalet-style timber architecture around Bariloche and the Lake District (San Carlos de Bariloche was heavily shaped by German/Swiss/Austrian immigrants); simple isolated sheep estancias scattered across the open steppe elsewhere.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Warm wood tones in the Alpine-influenced lake district; muted, weathered tones on remote steppe buildings.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Alpine chalet-style architecture in Bariloche; isolated sheep estancias; glacier and mountain-lodge infrastructure near El Calafate/El Chaltén; almost no dense urban development outside a handful of towns.

nature.vegetation: Dry steppe dominated by low grasses, shrubs and cushion plants, with very few trees — huge, empty, windswept landscapes; temperate forest and glaciers appear close to the Andes in the west (Los Glaciares, Nahuel Huapi).
nature.terrain: Vast, sparsely populated plateau stretching from about 37°S to the Drake Passage, framed by the Andes to the west with glaciers and jagged peaks (Fitz Roy, Perito Moreno Glacier); flatter steppe further east toward the Atlantic.
nature.climate_signature: Famously strong, near-constant wind; cold, dry, and sparse — one of the most visually empty landscapes in South America. Guanacos (wild llama relatives) are commonly visible grazing in herds.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: 4WD pickups more common given rough/unpaved rural roads (ripio gravel roads widespread).

google_coverage.camera_generation: Almost entirely Gen 3 with the black Google car — Argentina's Gen 4 coverage stops north of Comodoro Rivadavia, meaning nearly all of Patagonia is older Gen 3 imagery, a useful tell in itself.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Sparse — coverage concentrated on the few main highways (Ruta 40) and towns, with vast uncovered stretches in between.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Andes mountains, glaciers and windswept steppe straddling the same border region
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Chile's Patagonia sits on the wetter Pacific side with denser forest and a white-rear Google car look; Argentine Patagonia is drier steppe to the east of the Andes with the black Gen 3 car and Ruta 40's long straight gravel stretches.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script and plate style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Patagonia is dry windswept empty steppe with guanacos and glaciers; the Pampas is flat green farmland, and the northwest is colourful high-altitude desert — visually distinct from both.
